correctness.rationale: A fixed u-v path of length k is contained in (k+1)n^(n-k-2) labeled trees by the classical forest-extension formula. Adding any r prescribed off-path neighbors of u changes the path component size from k+1 to k+1+r and gives the exact inclusion probability ((k+1+r)/(k+1))n^(-r). Summing these probabilities yields the factored pgf. An explicit coupling proves strict stochastic decrease in k, and exact moment algebra gives the covariance identity and asymptotics.

value.rationale: Degree and graph distance are canonical local and global observables of uniform labeled trees. A complete conditional law and monotone-regression theorem provide substantially more information than separate marginal distributions, and the covariance/correlation asymptotics expose a non-obvious separation between order-one dependence and vanishing correlation.
